title: A Green Nomad above Giants
caption: Comet 252P/LINEAR above the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A soft green glow sits just above the Milky Way in this sweeping panorama, between the galaxy's starry arch and a Unit Telescope of ESO's Very Large Telescope at the center of the frame. That glow is Comet 252P/LINEAR, photographed in April 2016.

In late March 2016 this comet came closer to Earth than almost any comet on record, at just over 5.3 million kilometers. Halley's Comet, by comparison, came no closer than 87 million kilometers. Instead of a classic long tail, 252P/LINEAR shows a round glow tinted green by molecules of diatomic carbon fluorescing in sunlight.

The dark skies above Paranal offer much more. The Milky Way's clouds are crowded with stars, colorful natural airglow lines the horizon, and high overhead two planets join the red supergiant Antares in a slightly lopsided triangle, with bright Mars to the left and whitish Saturn below.

understand.summary: This is a panoramic landscape photograph taken with a camera at Paranal, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers more light than the eye, so the comet's green tint and the airglow near the horizon look far stronger than they would to an observer.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Paranal sits in the vast Atacama Desert under the dark southern sky, which makes it an excellent place to spot comets. ESO counts it among the most spectacular observatory sites on the planet.
alt: A panorama of the Milky Way arching over a telescope building, with a small green fuzzy comet just above the Milky Way and airglow along the horizon.
